title: Azure Subscriptions and Resource Groups
description: Understand Azure subscriptions, resource groups, and the management group hierarchy that keeps your cloud resources organized.

data.text: Before you can create anything in Azure, you need to understand how Azure organizes and tracks your resources. The three key concepts are **management groups**, **subscriptions**, and **resource groups**.

Management groups sit at the top of the hierarchy. They let you organize subscriptions into groups so you can apply policies and access controls across many subscriptions at once. For example, you might have a management group for 'Development' and another for 'Production'.

A subscription is a logical container for your Azure resources. It is linked to a billing account, and every resource you create in Azure must belong to a subscription. Subscriptions also set limits (quotas) on how many resources of each type you can create.

data.title: Common Subscription Types
items: **Free Trial** — 12 months of popular services free, plus $200 credit for the first 30 days
**Pay-As-You-Go** — billed monthly for what you use, no commitment
**Visual Studio Subscription** — monthly Azure credit for developers with an active VS subscription
**Enterprise Agreement** — for large organizations, negotiated pricing

data.text: A resource group is a container that holds related resources for an Azure solution. For example, a website might have a virtual machine, a database, and a storage account — all placed in the same resource group. Resource groups make it easy to deploy, update, and delete everything together.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Management groups organize subscriptions for enterprise governance
Subscriptions are billing and quota boundaries
Resource groups hold related resources for easier management
The Azure Free Account gives you 12 months of popular services plus $200 credit
data.takeaway: Understanding the hierarchy — management groups, subscriptions, resource groups — is essential for organizing and controlling Azure resources.
